prompt: Why did Steve Jobs leave NeXT?
response:
Steve Jobs did not leave NeXT because of any failure or dissatisfaction with the company itself. In fact, he founded NeXT in 1985 after he was ousted from Apple, the company he co-founded. NeXT was a computer company that developed and sold high-performance workstations and later focused on software development tools and web servers.

Jobs left NeXT in 1997, but not in the traditional sense of leaving the company. What actually happened was that Apple acquired NeXT in 1997 for $429 million. This acquisition was a strategic move by Apple to bring Jobs back into the company. At the time, Apple was struggling and was in need of a turnaround. Jobs returned to Apple as an advisor to the CEO, and later became the interim CEO, eventually leading Apple to unprecedented success.

So, to clarify, Steve Jobs didn't leave NeXT; rather, NeXT was acquired by Apple, which brought Jobs back to the company he co-founded.
